title: The ideal sheaf of a closed immersion
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $i:Z\to X$ a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. The *ideal sheaf* of $i$ (the sheaf of ideals defining the closed subscheme $Z$ of $X$) is the kernel $\mathcal I=\ker(i^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)\subset\mathcal O_X$; for an open $U\subseteq X$, $\mathcal I(U)=\ker(\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_Z(i^{-1}U))$. On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], where $i^{-1}(U)\to U$ is identified with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ for an ideal $I\subseteq R$, one has $\mathcal I(U)=I$ and $\mathcal I|_U=\widetilde I$; in particular $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, determined by its ideals $\mathcal I(U)\subseteq\mathcal O_X(U)$ on the affine opens $U$ of $X$.
